events.text:
Chinese intelligence support has helped Iran improve its ability to target U.S. ships and military bases in the Middle East, according to U.S. intelligence assessments.
Satellite imagery and geospatial data from Chinese groups helped Iran carry out a precise July strike on a U.S. base in Jordan that killed three American service members, officials said. 
The data has also improved Iran’s ability to track ships in the Strait of Hormuz and increase the effectiveness of drone and missile attacks.
U.S. officials say the extent of China’s involvement remains unclear, including whether Beijing directly ordered the support or merely allowed it. Russia has also provided assistance, while Iran’s battlefield experience has further improved its capabilities.
Source: CNN

events.text:
Russian state news agency RIA Novosti published and later deleted an article threatening Lithuania with a “short” war and possible nuclear strikes.
The article, titled “Russia faces another special military operation. It will be very short,” discussed scenarios of missile attacks on Lithuania.
The author, Alexander Nosovich, argued that Russia could use missiles with nuclear warheads instead of ground forces, claiming that a conflict in the Baltics would be quick due to geography.
RIA Novosti removed the article several hours after publication, later stating that it did not reflect the editorial line, editorial policy, or state policy of Russia.

events.text:
Two IDF reservists were killed yesterday after a small explosive drone they were operating in the Gaza Strip crashed for an unknown reason and exploded shortly after, the military announces.
The troops are named as Master Sgt. (res.) Nadav Kali, 24, from Har Halutz, and Master Sgt. (res.) Ofek Moalem, 23, from Jerusalem. 
Both served in the Jerusalem Brigade's 7007th Battalion.
According to a preliminary investigation by the military, the two soldiers on Thursday afternoon had been operating first-person view (FPV) drones known as "Atalef" -- Hebrew for bat -- from an army post inside the military's Gaza buffer zone in the Strip's north.
A first drone carried out its intended mission, while a second, during its takeoff, crashed inside the army post for an as-yet-unknown reason. The soldiers approached the crashed drone several minutes later, picked it up, and it then exploded, fatally wounding them, according to the initial probe.
The pair were taken to Barzilai Hospital in Ashkelon, where their deaths were declared.
Amid the investigation into the cause of the crash and explosion, the military has temporarily grounded all small drones capable of carrying explosive payloads -- both suicide drones and those that drop their explosives on a target.

🪖💣 UK military mulls adopting ‘stealth cavalry’ to beat killer drones
The British Army has come up with a new solution to drones that make short work of armored vehicles on the battlefield – soldiers on horseback
As the British military tested whether cavalry could move covertly through wooded terrain, Lieutenant-Colonel Ben McNeil told the Times that “a horse can move in a more natural profile than any armored vehicle can” and that it can be mistaken for wildlife while moving through woods.
👉 British media also boasts that horses have lower thermal signature than armored vehicles and thus can more easily escape detection by drone operators.
It is unclear whether the UK military officials realize that modern thermal-imaging gear can detect people and animals, or that a group of horseback riders moving in formation would hardly pass as a pack of animals.
And it seems that footage of drones stalking and taking out troop formations and individual soldiers, who are much harder to spot than a horse rider, completely eluded them.

events.text:
⛴ Is NATO hyping fake ‘Russia threat’ to justify seizing more Russian merchant vessels?
Deaf to Russia’s assurances that it [has no intention](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72009) of attacking anyone, the West is suddenly amplifying a highly specific and conveniently timed scenario.
US intelligence has warned several European governments that Russia may be preparing a drone operation against Spain, France or Italy, El Mundo reports. 
According to the pushed narrative, Russia could launch Gerbera drones - with a 600 km range and a speed of around 160 km/h - from merchant ships in the Mediterranean, potentially concealed in ordinary containers. 
The allegations could provide political cover for more aggressive interceptions of Russia-linked commercial ships under the banner of “self-defense.”
👉 There is precedent (under sanctions-enforcement rationale), such as US seizure of Russian-flagged Marinera in the North Atlantic in January, or UK boarding of Russia-linked tanker Smyrtos in June – slammed by Russia as "piracy and robbery".
NATO’s heightened military activity also feeds into this scenario.
The UK-led Strike Warrior 26 exercises are underway in waters north and east of Britain, involving carrier operations, anti-submarine warfare, air defense and live weapons training.
The drills cover approaches linking the North Sea, North Atlantic and Arctic, including maritime routes critical to Russia’s Northern Fleet and commercial shipping.

🇺🇸🪖 US military activity near Strait of Hormuz indicates possible new attack wave
US reconnaissance aircraft operated over Iran’s Qeshm and Hengam islands in the Strait of Hormuz overnight from Wednesday into Thursday, signaling increased military activity in the region, according to sources.
Additional US aircraft were reportedly observed conducting reconnaissance flights over Iran’s Kermanshah province, alongside unmanned aerial vehicles. The sources also said that twelve F-16 fighter jets had been deployed from Spangdahlem Air Base in Germany to the region.
FlightRadar data showed several types of US military aircraft operating or being deployed toward the area, including:
🌏 KC-135 Stratotanker aerial refueling aircraft
🌏 KC-46 Pegasus tanker aircraft
🌏 MQ-4C Triton surveillance drones
🌏 C-17 military transport aircraft  
The reported movements come after US President Donald Trump floated the idea of  “annihilating Iran” during his speech at the UNGA.
